text:
Alyssa: Heads-up — MarketPulse is seeing apparently 'shifted' scores from /v2/rerank when they send a multi-query batch. They say query 3's scores look like query 2's. Payload + response below, customer in prod so high priority.

Devon: Can you paste the exact request + response (redact keys) and a minimal repro?

Alyssa: Pasting sanitized payload and server response snippet. Note: they use nested per-query candidate lists, and one query intentionally has an empty candidates array.

Alyssa: ```json
# curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/rerank 
# -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
{
  "requests": [
    {"query": "Find pricing docs", "candidates": ["/docs/pricing.md","/docs/plan.md","/kb/pricing-info"]},
    {"query": "Get onboarding steps", "candidates": []},
    {"query": "API auth issues", "candidates": ["/docs/auth","/kb/tokens"]}
  ]
}
```

Alyssa: Response (sanitized):

```json
{
  "results": [
    {"scores": [0.9,0.75,0.6]},
    {"scores": [0.8,0.4]},    # <-- this is wrong: second query should be empty
    {"scores": [0.5,0.3]}     # looks like these belong to query 2 in reality
  ]
}
```

Maria: Hmm — empty per-query lists are an edge case. If the server flattens all candidates to a single array and uses offsets, an empty list can cause incorrect offsets if we don't emit a zero-length boundary. Have we validated candidate-length vectors server-side?

Samir: I reproduced locally. Our flattening code computes prefix sums but skips entries for empty vectors, then writes offsets into a buffer that expects a boundary for every request. Off-by-one when chunking.

support-bot: Ticket INC-41234 created (severity: P1). Notifying eng-runtime.

Devon: Can you try this minimal repro which isolates the empty-list case?

Devon: ```json
{
  "requests": [
    {"query": "q1", "candidates": ["a","b"]},
    {"query": "q2", "candidates": []},
    {"query": "q3", "candidates": ["c"]}
  ]
}
```

Alyssa: Repro steps I ran against staging: curl above -> response has q3 score returned as if for q2. Request-id: rwd-9876, ts=1987654321. I attached the raw response and request id to the ticket.

Maria: Short-term mitigation: clients can send an explicit placeholder in empty candidate arrays (eg. null or an empty string) and filter on client side after scoring. Not great but prevents shifts. We should document this until patched.

Samir: I'll push a hotfix to the flattening routine to always emit boundaries for empty lists and add a unit test. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/204 (WIP). ETA ~2h to land to canary.

Devon: Also add an input validator in the API layer returning 400 if the candidate-length vector is inconsistent with offsets (defensive). Put it in the same release window.

Alyssa: I'll update customer with repro, workaround, and ETA. Assigning follow-up to Samir.

support-bot: Customer notified via email. Next status update in 2h or sooner when patch lands.

Samir: After the fix I'll add a fuzz test for mixed empty/non-empty candidate lists and a regression test for the packing code.

Devon: Good. Also add a brief note in release notes: "Fix: batch rerank offsets when per-query candidate lists contain empty arrays".

Alyssa: Thanks all — will ping once customer acknowledges the mitigation. :thumbsup:
